source.text: וּֽלְנָעֳמִ֞י מוֹדַ֣ע לְאִישָׁ֗הּ אִ֚ישׁ גִּבּ֣וֹר חַ֔יִל מִמִּשְׁפַּ֖חַת אֱלִימֶ֑לֶךְ וּשְׁמ֖וֹ בֹּֽעַז׃

records.literal_gloss: And to Naomi [was] a relative of her husband, a man mighty of wealth, from [the] clan of Elimelech, and his name [was] Boaz.

en.L: Now Naomi had a relative of her husband, a man mighty in wealth, from the clan of Elimelech, and his name [was] Boaz.
en.B: Naomi had a relative on her husband's side, a man of wealth and standing from the clan of Elimelech. His name was Boaz.
en.R: Naomi had a relative on her husband's side named Boaz. He was a rich and respected man from Elimelech's clan.

sw.L: Naye Naomi alikuwa na jamaa wa mumewe, mtu hodari wa mali, wa ukoo wa Elimeleki, na jina lake [lilikuwa] Boazi.
sw.B: Naomi alikuwa na jamaa wa upande wa mumewe, mtu mwenye mali na heshima, wa ukoo wa Elimeleki. Jina lake lilikuwa Boazi.
sw.R: Naomi alikuwa na jamaa wa upande wa mumewe aitwaye Boazi. Alikuwa mtu tajiri na mwenye heshima wa ukoo wa Elimeleki.

es.L: Y Noemí tenía un pariente de su marido, un hombre poderoso en riqueza, del clan de Elimelec, y su nombre [era] Booz.
es.B: Noemí tenía un pariente por parte de su marido, un hombre rico e influyente del clan de Elimelec. Se llamaba Booz.
es.R: Noemí tenía un pariente por parte de su esposo que se llamaba Booz. Era un hombre rico y respetado del clan de Elimelec.

fr.L: Or Noémi avait un parent de son mari, un homme puissant en richesse, du clan d’Élimélek, et son nom [était] Booz.
fr.B: Noémi avait, du côté de son mari, un parent riche et considéré, du clan d’Élimélek. Il s’appelait Booz.
fr.R: Noémi avait, du côté de son mari, un parent qui s’appelait Booz. C’était un homme riche et respecté, du clan d’Élimélek.

vi.L: Na-ô-mi có một người bà con bên chồng, là một người giàu có và quyền thế, thuộc gia tộc Ê-li-mê-léc, tên [là] Bô-ô.
vi.B: Na-ô-mi có một người bà con bên chồng, là người giàu có và có địa vị, thuộc gia tộc Ê-li-mê-léc. Người ấy tên là Bô-ô.
vi.R: Na-ô-mi có một người bà con bên chồng tên là Bô-ô. Ông là một người giàu có và được kính trọng, thuộc gia tộc của Ê-li-mê-léc.

ko.L: 나오미에게는 남편 쪽 친척이 하나 있었는데, 그는 엘리멜렉 가문에 속한 큰 재력가였고, 그의 이름은 보아스였다.
ko.B: 나오미에게는 남편 쪽으로 친척이 하나 있었다. 그는 엘리멜렉 가문에 속한 사람으로, 재산도 많고 존경도 받는 사람이었다. 그의 이름은 보아스였다.
ko.R: 나오미에게는 남편 쪽으로 보아스라는 친척이 있었다. 그는 엘리멜렉 집안 사람이었고, 부자였으며 사람들에게 존경을 받았다.

pt.L: E Noemi tinha um parente do seu marido, um homem poderoso, de valor, do clã de Elimeleque, e o seu nome [era] Boaz.
pt.B: Noemi tinha um parente do lado do marido, um homem de valor, rico e respeitado, do clã de Elimeleque. O nome dele era Boaz.
pt.R: Noemi tinha um parente do lado do marido chamado Boaz. Ele era um homem de valor, rico e respeitado, do clã de Elimeleque.

am.L: ለኑኃሚንም የባሏ ዘመድ ነበራት፤ እርሱም ከአቤሜሌክ ጎሳ የሆነ በሀብት ብርቱ ሰው ነበረ፤ ስሙም ቦዔዝ [ነበረ]።
am.B: ኑኃሚን በባሏ በኩል ዘመድ ነበራት፤ እርሱም ከአቤሜሌክ ጎሳ የሆነ ሀብታምና የተከበረ ሰው ነበረ። ስሙም ቦዔዝ ይባል ነበር።
am.R: ኑኃሚን በባሏ በኩል ቦዔዝ የሚባል ዘመድ ነበራት። እርሱም ከአቤሜሌክ ጎሳ የሆነ ሀብታምና የተከበረ ሰው ነበረ።

decisions.choice: a man mighty in wealth: a man of substance and good name
decisions.reason: The phrase can describe a strong warrior (Judges 6:12; 11:1), but here, in a story of fields and harvest, it means a man of wealth, ability and standing in his town. The same word chayil is used of Ruth in 3:11, "a woman of worth", so the two are matched before they meet.

decisions.choice: relative: one known to the family, a kinsman
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text and the reading tradition give two slightly different forms of this word here, but both name a man close to the family: a relative or one known as kin. A word from the same root names Boaz as "our relative" in 3:2. Verse 20 shows how close he is.

decisions.choice: the narrator tells the reader first
decisions.reason: The verse interrupts the story to introduce Boaz before Ruth meets him. The reader knows who owns the field in verse 3; Ruth and Naomi do not learn it until verse 19.

decisions.choice: a man of wealth and standing (Balanced); a rich and respected man (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give both sides of the phrase, his wealth and his good name. Literal keeps "mighty in wealth".

decisions.choice: "Bô-ô" for Boaz
decisions.reason: The form published in Matthew 1:5, which the Joshua–Ruth terms note says wins.

decisions.choice: um homem poderoso, de valor (L); um homem de valor, rico e respeitado (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: chayil (m1) is wealth, ability and good name together, and it is the word used of Ruth in 3:11. Portuguese "valor" holds the same range (worth, means and courage), so every level says "de valor" here, and Ruth in 3:11 is "uma mulher de valor" (L) and "uma mulher virtuosa, de valor" (B, R), keeping the two matched; Balanced and Readable add "rico e respeitado", the two sides the English gives.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic, in Ruth 2 as in Ruth 1
decisions.reason: The English offers capitalised pronouns for God as a reader setting (in 2:12 and 2:20). The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so in Amharic the setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: "በሀብት ብርቱ ሰው" (Literal), so that "ብርቱ ሴት" for Ruth in 3:11 answers it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew calls Boaz a man of ḥayil here and Ruth a woman of ḥayil in 3:11. Literal gives both the same Amharic word so the match can be seen; Balanced and Readable say what the phrase means ("ሀብታምና የተከበረ").

source.text: וַתֹּאמֶר֩ ר֨וּת הַמּוֹאֲבִיָּ֜ה אֶֽל־נָעֳמִ֗י אֵֽלְכָה־נָּ֤א הַשָּׂדֶה֙ וַאֲלַקֳטָּ֣הבַשִׁבֳּלִ֔יםאַחַ֕ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶמְצָא־חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינָ֑יו וַתֹּ֥אמֶר לָ֖הּ לְכִ֥י בִתִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Ruth the Moabite to Naomi, let me go, please, [to] the field and let me glean among the ears behind [one] who I find favor in his eyes. And she said to her, go, my daughter.

en.L: And Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, "Please let me go to the field and glean among the ears of grain behind [someone] in whose eyes I find favor." And she said to her, "Go, my daughter."
en.B: Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, "Let me go out to the fields and glean ears of grain behind anyone who will look on me with favor." Naomi answered her, "Go, my daughter."
en.R: Ruth, the woman from Moab, said to Naomi, "Let me go out to the fields. I will pick up the grain the harvesters leave behind, if someone will be kind enough to let me." Naomi said to her, "Go ahead, my daughter."

sw.L: Naye Ruthu Mmoabu akamwambia Naomi, "Tafadhali niache niende shambani niokote masazo kati ya masuke nyuma ya [mtu] ambaye nitapata kibali machoni pake." Naye akamwambia, "Nenda, binti yangu."
sw.B: Ruthu Mmoabu alimwambia Naomi, "Niache niende mashambani niokote masazo ya masuke nyuma ya yeyote atakayenitazama kwa kibali." Naomi akamjibu, "Nenda, binti yangu."
sw.R: Ruthu, yule mwanamke wa Moabu, alimwambia Naomi, "Niache niende mashambani. Nitaokota nafaka ambayo wavunaji wanaiacha nyuma, kama kuna mtu atakayekuwa mwema kiasi cha kuniruhusu." Naomi alimwambia, "Haya nenda, binti yangu."

es.L: Y Rut la moabita dijo a Noemí: «Déjame ir, te ruego, al campo, y recogeré espigas detrás de [aquel] a cuyos ojos halle gracia». Y ella le dijo: «Ve, hija mía».
es.B: Rut la moabita le dijo a Noemí: «Déjame ir a los campos a recoger espigas detrás de quien me mire con favor». Noemí le respondió: «Ve, hija mía».
es.R: Rut, la mujer de Moab, le dijo a Noemí: «Déjame ir a los campos. Recogeré el grano que dejan atrás los segadores, si alguien es tan amable de permitírmelo». Noemí le dijo: «Anda, hija mía».

fr.L: Et Ruth la Moabite dit à Noémi : « Laisse-moi donc aller aux champs et glaner parmi les épis derrière [quelqu’un] aux yeux de qui je trouverai grâce. » Et elle lui dit : « Va, ma fille. »
fr.B: Ruth la Moabite dit à Noémi : « Laisse-moi aller aux champs glaner des épis derrière quelqu’un qui me regardera avec bienveillance. » Noémi lui répondit : « Va, ma fille. »
fr.R: Ruth, la femme de Moab, a dit à Noémi : « Laisse-moi aller dans les champs. Je ramasserai les épis que les moissonneurs laissent derrière eux, si quelqu’un veut bien me le permettre. » Noémi lui a dit : « Vas-y, ma fille. »

vi.L: Ru-tơ người Mô-áp nói với Na-ô-mi: "Xin mẹ cho con ra đồng mót bông lúa sau người nào mà con được ơn trước mắt người ấy." Bà nói với nàng: "Con gái của mẹ, hãy đi đi."
vi.B: Ru-tơ người Mô-áp nói với Na-ô-mi: "Xin mẹ để con ra đồng mót bông lúa theo sau người nào có lòng tốt với con." Na-ô-mi đáp: "Con gái của mẹ, con cứ đi."
vi.R: Ru-tơ, người phụ nữ Mô-áp, nói với Na-ô-mi: "Xin mẹ để con ra đồng. Con sẽ nhặt những bông lúa người gặt bỏ sót lại, nếu có ai tốt bụng cho phép con." Na-ô-mi nói với nàng: "Con cứ đi đi, con gái của mẹ."

ko.L: 모압 여자 룻이 나오미에게 말했다. "부디 제가 밭에 나가서, 저에게 호의를 베푸는 사람의 뒤를 따라 이삭을 줍게 해 주세요." 나오미가 그에게 말했다. "가거라, 내 딸아."
ko.B: 모압 여자 룻이 나오미에게 말했다. "밭에 나가서, 저를 너그럽게 봐주는 사람이 있으면 그 사람 뒤를 따라 이삭을 줍게 해 주세요." 나오미가 대답했다. "그래, 가거라, 내 딸아."
ko.R: 모압에서 온 룻이 나오미에게 말했다. "밭에 나가 볼게요. 누가 친절하게 허락해 주면, 일꾼들이 거두고 남긴 이삭을 주울게요." 나오미가 말했다. "그래, 가거라, 내 딸아."

pt.L: E Rute, a moabita, disse a Noemi: "Deixe-me ir ao campo, por favor, e respigar entre as espigas atrás [de alguém] aos olhos de quem eu encontre favor." E ela lhe disse: "Vá, minha filha."
pt.B: Rute, a moabita, disse a Noemi: "Deixe-me ir aos campos respigar espigas atrás de alguém que me olhe com bondade." Noemi lhe respondeu: "Vá, minha filha."
pt.R: Rute, a mulher de Moabe, disse a Noemi: "Deixe-me ir aos campos. Vou apanhar as espigas que os ceifeiros deixarem para trás, se alguém tiver a bondade de me deixar fazer isso." Noemi respondeu: "Pode ir, minha filha."

am.L: ሞዓባዊቱ ሩትም ኑኃሚንን፦ «እባክሽ፣ ወደ እርሻ ልሂድ፤ በዓይኑ ሞገስ የማገኘውን [ሰው] ተከትዬ ከዛላዎቹ መካከል ልቃርም» አለቻት። እርሷም፦ «ልጄ ሆይ፣ ሂጂ» አለቻት።
am.B: ሞዓባዊቱ ሩት ኑኃሚንን፦ «በደግነት የሚመለከተኝን ማንኛውንም ሰው ተከትዬ ዛላ ለመቃረም ወደ እርሻ ልውጣ» አለቻት። ኑኃሚንም፦ «ልጄ፣ ሂጂ» ብላ መለሰችላት።
am.R: ከሞዓብ የመጣችው ሩት ኑኃሚንን፦ «ወደ እርሻ ልውጣ። አንድ ሰው ደግ ሆኖ ቢፈቅድልኝ፣ አጫጆቹ ትተውት የሚሄዱትን እህል እለቅማለሁ» አለቻት። ኑኃሚንም፦ «ልጄ፣ በይ ሂጂ» አለቻት።

decisions.choice: glean: gather the grain the harvesters left behind
decisions.reason: God's law told landowners not to reap to the very edges of a field or go back for what was dropped or forgotten, but to leave it for the poor, the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow (Leviticus 19:9-10; 23:22; Deuteronomy 24:19). Ruth is poor, foreign and widowed, so she has a right to glean.

decisions.choice: find favor in his eyes: be treated kindly
decisions.reason: To find favor in someone's eyes is to win his goodwill. Even with the law on her side, Ruth hopes to find a landowner or reaper who will let her glean and treat her well; the same phrase comes back in verses 10 and 13.

decisions.choice: Ruth the Moabite: her foreign origin kept in view
decisions.reason: The narrator keeps calling her "the Moabite" (1:22; 2:21) and others do too (verse 6). The story never lets the reader forget that a foreign woman is the one who shows such loyalty.

decisions.choice: pick up the grain the harvesters leave behind, if someone will be kind enough to let me
decisions.reason: Readable explains what gleaning is and says what "finding favor" means here: someone letting her glean.

decisions.choice: "kuokota masazo" (to pick up what is left) for gleaning; Readable "kuokota nafaka ambayo wavunaji wanaiacha nyuma"
decisions.reason: Swahili has no single verb for gleaning; "masazo" are the leftovers, and Readable spells out the custom (m1), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Naomi calls Ruth "binti yangu" (my daughter); Ruth speaks to her with the singular "wewe"
decisions.reason: As Ruth 1, the affectionate word of an older woman to a younger; Boaz uses the same words to Ruth in verse 8 (m2 there).

decisions.choice: "recoger espigas"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb means gathering the grain the harvesters left behind (m1); "recoger espigas" is the Spanish phrase for it, and Readable explains it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "glaner" (L, B); "ramasser les épis que les moissonneurs laissent" (R)
decisions.reason: "Glaner" is the exact French word for gathering the grain the harvesters leave (m1), and it is kept at Literal and Balanced through the chapter. Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does, since young readers may not know the word.

decisions.choice: "mót" for "glean"
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese word for gathering what harvesters leave behind, exactly the practice the law allowed the poor (meaning decision); Readable describes it as well.

decisions.choice: respigar (L, B); apanhar as espigas que os ceifeiros deixarem para trás (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: "respigar" is the Portuguese verb for gleaning, the word of the gleaning laws in Leviticus 19:9 in Portuguese (m1). Readable explains it, as the English Readable does, and says "apanhar espigas" afterwards. The reapers are "os ceifeiros" at every level.

decisions.choice: glean: "መቃረም" (Literal, Balanced), "እህል መልቀም" (Readable), through the book; ears of grain "ዛላ"
decisions.reason: "ቃርሚያ" and "መቃረም" are the Amharic words for gathering what the harvesters leave, as the terms list has it; Readable uses the everyday "መልቀም" (pick up) with what is picked up spelled out, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וַתֵּ֤לֶךְ וַתָּבוֹא֙ וַתְּלַקֵּ֣ט בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה אַחֲרֵ֖י הַקֹּצְרִ֑ים וַיִּ֣קֶר מִקְרֶ֔הָ חֶלְקַ֤ת הַשָּׂדֶה֙ לְבֹ֔עַז אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִמִּשְׁפַּ֥חַת אֱלִימֶֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she went and came and gleaned in the field behind the harvesters; and chanced her chance [on the] portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who [was] from [the] clan of Elimelech.

en.L: So she went and came and gleaned in the field behind the harvesters, and her chance chanced upon the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who [was] from the clan of Elimelech.
en.B: So she set out, came to a field and gleaned behind the harvesters. As it happened, she came to the part of the field that belonged to Boaz, who was from the clan of Elimelech.
en.R: So Ruth went out and began picking up grain behind the harvesters. It just so happened that she was working in a field that belonged to Boaz, the man from Elimelech's clan.

sw.L: Naye akaenda, akafika, akaokota masazo shambani nyuma ya wavunaji; na bahati yake ikamwangukia sehemu ya shamba iliyokuwa ya Boazi, aliyekuwa wa ukoo wa Elimeleki.
sw.B: Basi aliondoka, akafika shambani, akaokota masazo nyuma ya wavunaji. Ikatukia kwamba alifika katika sehemu ya shamba iliyokuwa ya Boazi, aliyekuwa wa ukoo wa Elimeleki.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Ruthu alikwenda, akaanza kuokota nafaka nyuma ya wavunaji. Ikatukia tu kwamba alikuwa akifanya kazi katika shamba lililokuwa la Boazi, yule mtu wa ukoo wa Elimeleki.

es.L: Y fue, y llegó y recogió espigas en el campo detrás de los segadores; y quiso su suerte que [diera con] la parcela del campo que pertenecía a Booz, que [era] del clan de Elimelec.
es.B: Así que salió, llegó a un campo y se puso a recoger espigas detrás de los segadores. Y dio la casualidad de que llegó a la parte del campo que pertenecía a Booz, que era del clan de Elimelec.
es.R: Así que Rut salió y comenzó a recoger grano detrás de los segadores. Y resultó que estaba trabajando en un campo que pertenecía a Booz, el hombre del clan de Elimelec.

fr.L: Et elle s’en alla, et elle vint et glana dans le champ derrière les moissonneurs ; et son sort la fit tomber sur la parcelle du champ qui appartenait à Booz, qui [était] du clan d’Élimélek.
fr.B: Elle partit donc et alla glaner dans un champ derrière les moissonneurs. Il se trouva qu’elle arriva dans la parcelle qui appartenait à Booz, du clan d’Élimélek.
fr.R: Ruth est donc partie, et elle a commencé à ramasser des épis derrière les moissonneurs. Il s’est trouvé que c’était dans un champ qui appartenait à Booz, l’homme du clan d’Élimélek.

vi.L: Nàng đi đến ruộng và mót lúa sau những người gặt; và may thay, nàng tình cờ đến phần ruộng thuộc về Bô-ô, người thuộc gia tộc Ê-li-mê-léc.
vi.B: Vậy nàng ra đi, đến một cánh đồng và mót lúa sau những người gặt. Tình cờ nàng đến đúng phần ruộng thuộc về Bô-ô, người thuộc gia tộc Ê-li-mê-léc.
vi.R: Vậy Ru-tơ ra đồng và bắt đầu nhặt lúa sau những người gặt. Thật tình cờ, nàng làm việc trong cánh đồng của Bô-ô, người thuộc gia tộc của Ê-li-mê-léc.

ko.L: 룻이 가서 밭에 이르러 거두는 사람들 뒤를 따라 이삭을 주웠다. 그런데 우연히도 그가 이른 곳이 엘리멜렉 가문에 속한 보아스의 밭이었다.
ko.B: 그래서 룻은 길을 나서서 어느 밭에 이르러 일꾼들 뒤를 따라 이삭을 주웠다. 그런데 마침 그가 간 곳은 엘리멜렉 가문 사람인 보아스의 밭이었다.
ko.R: 그래서 룻은 밭에 나가서 일꾼들 뒤를 따라다니며 이삭을 줍기 시작했다. 그런데 마침 그 밭은 엘리멜렉 집안 사람인 보아스의 밭이었다.

pt.L: E ela foi, e chegou, e respigou no campo atrás dos ceifeiros; e o seu acaso a fez cair na parte do campo que pertencia a Boaz, que [era] do clã de Elimeleque.
pt.B: Ela saiu, chegou a um campo e respigou atrás dos ceifeiros. Por acaso, foi parar na parte do campo que pertencia a Boaz, que era do clã de Elimeleque.
pt.R: Rute foi e começou a apanhar espigas atrás dos ceifeiros. E aconteceu, por acaso, que ela estava trabalhando num campo que pertencia a Boaz, o homem do clã de Elimeleque.

am.L: ሄደችም፤ ገብታም ከአጫጆቹ በኋላ በእርሻው ቃረመች። አጋጣሚዋም ከአቤሜሌክ ጎሳ የሆነው የቦዔዝ ወደሆነው የእርሻ ክፍል አደረሳት።
am.B: ስለዚህ ሄደች፤ ወደ አንድ እርሻ ደርሳ ከአጫጆቹ በኋላ ቃረመች። እንደ አጋጣሚ የደረሰችውም ከአቤሜሌክ ጎሳ የሆነው የቦዔዝ ወደሆነው የእርሻ ክፍል ነበረ።
am.R: ስለዚህ ሩት ወጥታ ከአጫጆቹ በኋላ እህል መልቀም ጀመረች። የምትሠራበትም እርሻ በአጋጣሚ ከአቤሜሌክ ጎሳ የሆነው የቦዔዝ እርሻ ሆነ።

decisions.choice: her chance chanced: it happened, as far as she knew, by chance
decisions.reason: The verb and its noun come from the same root, a doubled way of saying it just happened. From Ruth's point of view it was luck. The narrator, who has already introduced Boaz (verse 1), lets the reader see more: Naomi will praise the LORD for it in verse 20.

decisions.choice: the portion of the field: one family's plot
decisions.reason: The farmland around a town was one open stretch divided into family plots without fences. A gleaner could move from one owner's strip to another without knowing whose land she was on.

decisions.choice: as it happened (Balanced); it just so happened (Readable)
decisions.reason: Both keep the sense of chance in plain words; Literal keeps the doubled Hebrew "her chance chanced".

decisions.choice: "우연히도" (as chance had it)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "her chance chanced", a doubled phrase. Korean cannot double it; Literal says "우연히도" and Balanced and Readable "마침", which keep the narrator's quiet hint that it was more than chance.

decisions.choice: o seu acaso a fez cair
decisions.reason: Portuguese has no verb from "acaso", so Literal keeps the doubled Hebrew of m1 by making "o seu acaso" the subject of the verb; Balanced and Readable say "por acaso", as the English does.

source.text: וְהִנֵּה־בֹ֗עַז בָּ֚א מִבֵּ֣ית לֶ֔חֶם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לַקּוֹצְרִ֖ים יְהוָ֣ה עִמָּכֶ֑ם וַיֹּ֥אמְרוּ ל֖וֹ יְבָרֶכְךָ֥ יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And look, Boaz [was] coming from Bethlehem and said to the harvesters, Yahweh [be] with you. And they said to him, may bless you Yahweh.

en.L: And look, Boaz came from Bethlehem and said to the harvesters, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [be] with you!" And they said to him, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you!"
en.B: Just then Boaz arrived from Bethlehem. He greeted the harvesters, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} be with you!" and they answered him, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you!"
en.R: Just then Boaz came out from Bethlehem. He said to the harvesters, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be with you!" They answered, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you!"

sw.L: Na tazama, Boazi akaja kutoka Bethlehemu, akawaambia wavunaji, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [na awe] pamoja nanyi!" Nao wakamwambia, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na akubariki!"
sw.B: Wakati huo huo Boazi alifika kutoka Bethlehemu. Aliwasalimu wavunaji, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} awe pamoja nanyi!" Nao wakamjibu, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akubariki!"
sw.R: Wakati huo huo Boazi alitoka Bethlehemu. Aliwaambia wavunaji, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} awe pamoja nanyi!" Nao wakajibu, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akubariki!"

es.L: Y he aquí, Booz vino de Belén y dijo a los segadores: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [sea] con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}». Y ellos le dijeron: «Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te bendiga».
es.B: En ese momento llegó Booz de Belén. Saludó a los segadores: «¡{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} sea con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}!». Y ellos le respondieron: «¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te bendiga!».
es.R: En ese momento llegó Booz de Belén. Les dijo a los segadores: «¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} esté con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}!». Ellos le respondieron: «¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te bendiga!».

fr.L: Et voici, Booz vint de Bethléem et dit aux moissonneurs : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [soit] avec vous ! » Et ils lui dirent : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} te bénisse ! »
fr.B: Juste à ce moment, Booz arriva de Bethléem. Il salua les moissonneurs : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} soit avec vous ! » Et ils lui répondirent : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} te bénisse ! »
fr.R: Juste à ce moment, Booz est arrivé de Bethléem. Il a dit aux moissonneurs : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} soit avec vous ! » Ils lui ont répondu : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} te bénisse ! »

vi.L: Và kìa, Bô-ô từ Bết-lê-hem đến và nói với những người gặt: "Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở cùng các anh!" Họ đáp: "Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban phước cho ông!"
vi.B: Ngay lúc ấy, Bô-ô từ Bết-lê-hem đến. Ông chào những người gặt: "Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở cùng các anh!" Họ đáp: "Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban phước cho ông!"
vi.R: Ngay lúc ấy, Bô-ô từ Bết-lê-hem đến. Ông nói với những người gặt: "Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở cùng các anh!" Họ đáp: "Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban phước cho ông!"

ko.L: 보라, 보아스가 베들레헴에서 와서 거두는 사람들에게 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희와 함께하시기를 바란다!" 그들이 그에게 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 주인님께 복을 주시기를 바랍니다!"
ko.B: 바로 그때 보아스가 베들레헴에서 왔다. 그는 일꾼들에게 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희와 함께하시기를 바란다!" 하고 인사했다. 그들도 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 주인님께 복을 주시기를 바랍니다!" 하고 대답했다.
ko.R: 바로 그때 보아스가 베들레헴에서 나왔다. 그는 일꾼들에게 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희와 함께하시기를 바란다!" 하고 말했다. 일꾼들도 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 주인님께 복을 주시기를 바랍니다!" 하고 대답했다.

pt.L: E eis que Boaz chegou de Belém e disse aos ceifeiros: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} [esteja] com vocês!" E eles lhe disseram: "Que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} o abençoe!"
pt.B: Nisso Boaz chegou de Belém. Ele saudou os ceifeiros: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} esteja com vocês!" E eles lhe responderam: "Que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} o abençoe!"
pt.R: Nisso Boaz chegou de Belém. Ele disse aos ceifeiros: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} esteja com vocês!" Eles responderam: "Que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} o abençoe!"

am.L: እነሆም፣ ቦዔዝ ከቤተ ልሔም መጣ፤ አጫጆቹንም፦ «{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ከእናንተ ጋር [ይሁን]» አላቸው። እነርሱም፦ «{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ይባርክዎ» አሉት።
am.B: በዚያን ጊዜ ቦዔዝ ከቤተ ልሔም ደረሰ። አጫጆቹንም፦ «{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ከእናንተ ጋር ይሁን!» ብሎ ሰላምታ ሰጣቸው፤ እነርሱም፦ «{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ይባርክዎ!» ብለው መለሱለት።
am.R: በዚያን ጊዜ ቦዔዝ ከቤተ ልሔም መጣ። አጫጆቹንም፦ «{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ከእናንተ ጋር ይሁን!» አላቸው። እነርሱም፦ «{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ይባርክዎ!» ብለው መለሱለት።

decisions.choice: and look: Boaz arrives at that very moment
decisions.reason: The word hinneh draws attention to what happens next, as if the reader were watching. Ruth has only just come to the field when its owner appears.

decisions.choice: greeting and reply as blessings
decisions.reason: People greeted one another with a blessing in the LORD's name (Judges 6:12; Psalm 129:8). The exchange shows a landowner and workers on good terms, and a man who speaks of God in everyday life.

decisions.choice: just then
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express hinneh by its timing; Literal keeps "look".

decisions.choice: Boaz greets his harvesters with "các anh"; they answer with "ông"
decisions.reason: A landowner greeting his workers kindly, and workers answering their employer with respect; the greeting and reply are both blessings (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: Boaz speaks to his workers in the plain style (해라체); they answer in the formal polite style (합쇼체) with "주인님"
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set for Boaz and his reapers, and for master and servant.

decisions.choice: "O SENHOR esteja com vocês!" "Que o SENHOR o abençoe!"
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Boaz greets his workers with "vocês", and they answer their master with "o", the pronoun that goes with "o senhor" (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4), as Ruth too speaks to him (verses 10, 13). The greeting keeps the LORD's name, which is the point of m2.

decisions.choice: the harvesters answer their master with the respectful "ይባርክዎ"
decisions.reason: Workers speaking to the landowner they serve use "እርስዎ", as servants to a master do through the Amharic Bible; Boaz greets them with the plain plural.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בֹּ֨עַז֙ לְנַעֲר֔וֹ הַנִּצָּ֖ב עַל־הַקּֽוֹצְרִ֑ים לְמִ֖י הַנַּעֲרָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Boaz to his young man, the [one] stationed over the harvesters, to whom [is] this young woman?

en.L: And Boaz said to his young man who was set over the harvesters, "To whom [does] this young woman [belong]?"
en.B: Boaz asked his servant who was in charge of the harvesters, "Whose young woman is this?"
en.R: Boaz asked the man in charge of his harvesters, "Who is that young woman? What family is she from?"

sw.L: Naye Boazi akamwambia kijana wake aliyesimamia wavunaji, "Msichana huyu ni wa nani?"
sw.B: Boazi alimwuliza mtumishi wake aliyekuwa msimamizi wa wavunaji, "Msichana huyu ni wa nani?"
sw.R: Boazi alimwuliza mtu aliyekuwa msimamizi wa wavunaji wake, "Msichana yule ni nani? Ni wa jamaa gani?"

es.L: Y Booz dijo a su muchacho, el que estaba puesto sobre los segadores: «¿De quién [es] esta joven?».
es.B: Booz le preguntó al criado que estaba a cargo de los segadores: «¿De quién es esta joven?».
es.R: Booz le preguntó al hombre que estaba a cargo de sus segadores: «¿Quién es esa joven? ¿De qué familia es?».

fr.L: Et Booz dit à son jeune homme qui était préposé aux moissonneurs : « À qui [est] cette jeune femme ? »
fr.B: Booz demanda à son serviteur qui surveillait les moissonneurs : « À qui appartient cette jeune femme ? »
fr.R: Booz a demandé à l’homme qui dirigeait ses moissonneurs : « Qui est cette jeune femme ? De quelle famille est-elle ? »

vi.L: Bô-ô nói với người đầy tớ trẻ của mình là người coi sóc những người gặt: "Thiếu nữ này thuộc về ai?"
vi.B: Bô-ô hỏi người đầy tớ coi sóc những người gặt: "Thiếu nữ này là người nhà ai vậy?"
vi.R: Bô-ô hỏi người coi sóc những người gặt của mình: "Thiếu nữ kia là ai vậy? Cô ấy thuộc gia đình nào?"

ko.L: 보아스가 거두는 사람들을 감독하는 자기의 젊은 종에게 말했다. "이 젊은 여자는 누구에게 속한 사람이냐?"
ko.B: 보아스가 일꾼들을 감독하는 종에게 물었다. "저 젊은 여자는 누구네 집 사람이냐?"
ko.R: 보아스가 일꾼들을 감독하는 사람에게 물었다. "저 젊은 여자는 누구냐? 어느 집안 사람이냐?"

pt.L: E Boaz disse ao seu moço, o que estava encarregado dos ceifeiros: "De quem [é] esta moça?"
pt.B: Boaz perguntou ao servo que estava encarregado dos ceifeiros: "De quem é esta moça?"
pt.R: Boaz perguntou ao homem que chefiava os seus ceifeiros: "Quem é aquela moça? De que família ela é?"

am.L: ቦዔዝም በአጫጆቹ ላይ የተሾመውን ብላቴናውን፦ «ይህች ወጣት ሴት የማን ናት?» አለው።
am.B: ቦዔዝም በአጫጆቹ ላይ ኃላፊ የሆነውን አገልጋዩን፦ «ይህች ወጣት ሴት የማን ናት?» ብሎ ጠየቀው።
am.R: ቦዔዝም የአጫጆቹን አለቃ፦ «ያቺ ወጣት ሴት ማን ናት? ከየትኛው ቤተሰብ ናት?» ብሎ ጠየቀው።

decisions.choice: his young man set over the harvesters: his foreman
decisions.reason: Na'ar means a young man, and often a young man in someone's service, a worker or attendant. This one has been put in charge of the reapers.

decisions.choice: to whom does she belong?: what household is she part of
decisions.reason: A woman was known by the household she belonged to: her father's, her husband's, or a master's. Boaz asks not her name but her family and place, and the answer in verse 6 tells him exactly that.

decisions.choice: young woman: na'arah
decisions.reason: The word is used of a girl or young woman, often unmarried and sometimes in service. Ruth is a widow but still young; Boaz is older (3:10).

decisions.choice: servant (Balanced); the man in charge (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "young man", the word's basic sense; Balanced and Readable say what he was to Boaz.

decisions.choice: What family is she from?
decisions.reason: Readable adds the second question to show what "whose" means here.

decisions.choice: a moça; as moças (verses 8, 22, 23); o moço (L), o servo (B), os rapazes (B, R for na'arim)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: na'arah (m3) is "moça", the ordinary word for a young woman, married or not, at every level; Boaz's young women are "as moças". The young men are "os moços" at Literal and "os rapazes" at Balanced and Readable; the foreman is "o seu moço" at Literal and "o servo" at Balanced, as the English says "servant".

decisions.choice: na'ar "ብላቴና" (Literal), "አገልጋይ" (Balanced); plural na'arim "ጎበዛዝት"; na'arah "ወጣት ሴት", Boaz's na'arot "ልጃገረዶች" (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew words are for young people who work in a household or field. "ብላቴና" is the Amharic word for a young male servant; "ገረድ" is kept for the maidservant Ruth calls herself (2:13; 3:9), so the reader can tell the two Hebrew words apart.

records.literal_gloss: And answered the young man, the [one] stationed over the harvesters, and said, a young woman, a Moabite, [is] she, the [one who] returned with Naomi from [the] field of Moab.

en.L: And the young man who was set over the harvesters answered and said, "She [is] a young Moabite woman, the [one] who returned with Naomi from the country of Moab.
en.B: The servant in charge of the harvesters answered, "She is a young Moabite woman, the one who came back with Naomi from the country of Moab.
en.R: The man answered, "She is the young woman from Moab who came back with Naomi.

sw.L: Naye yule kijana aliyesimamia wavunaji akajibu, akasema, "Yeye [ni] msichana Mmoabu, yule aliyerudi pamoja na Naomi kutoka nchi ya Moabu.
sw.B: Mtumishi aliyekuwa msimamizi wa wavunaji alijibu, "Yeye ni msichana Mmoabu, yule aliyerudi pamoja na Naomi kutoka nchi ya Moabu.
sw.R: Yule mtu alijibu, "Yeye ni yule msichana wa Moabu aliyerudi pamoja na Naomi.

es.B: El criado encargado de los segadores le respondió: «Es una joven moabita, la que volvió con Noemí de la región de Moab.
es.R: El hombre le contestó: «Es la joven de Moab que vino con Noemí.

pt.B: O servo encarregado dos ceifeiros respondeu: "Ela é uma moça moabita, aquela que voltou com Noemi da terra de Moabe.

decisions.choice: returned: came back with Naomi
decisions.reason: Ruth had never lived in Bethlehem, yet the same verb is used of her as of Naomi (1:22). By joining Naomi's people (1:16) she has, in a sense, come home with her.

decisions.choice: a young Moabite woman: her origin first
decisions.reason: The foreman's first words are that she is a Moabite. Moab and Israel had a hard history (Numbers 22-25; Deuteronomy 23:4-5), so this is the first thing people notice about her.

decisions.choice: the field of Moab: the country of Moab
decisions.reason: The word for field also means open country or territory, as in 1:1 and 1:6.

decisions.choice: from Moab ... came back with Naomi
decisions.reason: Readable says "from Moab" once, so the country is not named twice in one short sentence.

records.literal_gloss: And she said, let me glean, please, and I will gather among the sheaves behind the harvesters. And she came and has stood from then, the morning, and until now; this her sitting [in] the house [is a] little.

en.L: And she said, 'Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the harvesters.' So she came and has stood from the morning until now; her sitting in the house [has been] little."
en.B: She said, 'Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the harvesters.' So she came, and she has been on her feet from early morning until now, except for a short rest in the shelter."
en.R: She asked me, 'Please let me pick up grain among the bundles behind the harvesters.' She came early this morning, and she has been working ever since. She has only stopped for a little while to rest in the shelter."

sw.L: Naye alisema, 'Tafadhali niache niokote masazo na kukusanya kati ya miganda nyuma ya wavunaji.' Basi akaja, akasimama tangu asubuhi mpaka sasa; kukaa kwake nyumbani [kumekuwa] kidogo."
sw.B: Alisema, 'Tafadhali niache niokote masazo na kukusanya kati ya miganda nyuma ya wavunaji.' Kwa hiyo alikuja, naye amekuwa kazini tangu asubuhi na mapema mpaka sasa, ila tu alipumzika kidogo kibandani."
sw.R: Aliniomba, 'Tafadhali niache niokote nafaka kati ya mafungu nyuma ya wavunaji.' Alikuja asubuhi na mapema, naye amekuwa akifanya kazi tangu wakati huo. Amesimama tu kwa muda mfupi kupumzika kibandani."

es.L: Y dijo: “Déjame recoger espigas, te ruego, y juntar entre las gavillas detrás de los segadores”. Y vino y ha estado en pie desde la mañana hasta ahora; su descanso en la casa [ha sido] poco».
es.B: Me dijo: “Por favor, déjame recoger espigas y juntarlas entre las gavillas detrás de los segadores”. Así que vino, y ha estado de pie desde la mañana hasta ahora, salvo un breve descanso en el cobertizo».
es.R: Me pidió: “Por favor, déjame recoger grano entre los manojos, detrás de los segadores”. Vino temprano esta mañana y ha estado trabajando desde entonces. Solo se ha detenido un ratito para descansar en el cobertizo».

fr.L: Et elle a dit : “Laisse-moi glaner, je te prie, et ramasser parmi les gerbes derrière les moissonneurs.” Et elle est venue et elle est restée debout depuis le matin jusqu’à maintenant ; son repos dans la maison [a été] bref. »
fr.B: Elle m’a dit : “Permets-moi de glaner et de ramasser parmi les gerbes derrière les moissonneurs.” Elle est donc venue, et elle est restée debout depuis le matin jusqu’à maintenant, à part un court repos sous l’abri. »
fr.R: Elle m’a demandé : “S’il te plaît, laisse-moi ramasser des épis entre les gerbes, derrière les moissonneurs.” Elle est arrivée tôt ce matin, et elle travaille depuis. Elle s’est seulement arrêtée un petit moment pour se reposer sous l’abri. »

vi.R: Cô ấy xin tôi: 'Xin cho tôi nhặt lúa giữa các bó lúa sau những người gặt.' Cô ấy đến từ sáng sớm và làm việc suốt từ đó đến giờ. Cô ấy chỉ ngồi nghỉ một chút trong lều."

ko.B: 그 여자는 '일꾼들 뒤를 따라 단 사이에서 이삭을 줍고 모으게 해 주십시오' 하고 부탁했습니다. 그리고 이른 아침부터 지금까지 계속 일하고 있습니다. 쉼터에서 잠깐 쉬었을 뿐입니다."
ko.R: 그 여자가 저에게 '일꾼들 뒤를 따라다니며 곡식 단 사이에서 이삭을 줍게 해 주십시오' 하고 부탁했습니다. 그 여자는 아침 일찍 와서 지금까지 줄곧 일했습니다. 쉼터에서 잠깐 쉬었을 뿐입니다."

pt.B: Ela pediu: 'Por favor, deixe-me respigar e ajuntar espigas entre os feixes, atrás dos ceifeiros.' Ela veio e está trabalhando em pé desde cedo até agora, a não ser por um breve descanso no abrigo."
pt.R: Ela me pediu: 'Por favor, deixe-me apanhar espigas entre os feixes, atrás dos ceifeiros.' Ela chegou hoje cedo e está trabalhando desde então. Só parou um pouco para descansar no abrigo."

am.L: እርሷም፦ “እባክህ፣ ከአጫጆቹ በኋላ በነዶዎቹ መካከል ልቃርምና ልሰብስብ” አለች። መጥታም ከጠዋት ጀምሮ እስከ አሁን ድረስ ቆማለች፤ በቤትም መቀመጧ ጥቂት [ነበረ]።»
am.B: እርሷም፦ “እባክህ፣ ከአጫጆቹ በኋላ በነዶዎቹ መካከል ልቃርምና ልሰብስብ” አለች። ስለዚህ መጣች፤ በመጠለያው ውስጥ ለጥቂት ጊዜ ከማረፏ በቀር፣ ከማለዳ ጀምሮ እስከ አሁን ድረስ በሥራ ላይ ቆማለች።»
am.R: እርሷም፦ “እባክህ፣ ከአጫጆቹ በኋላ በነዶዎቹ መካከል እህል ልልቀም” ብላ ጠየቀችኝ። ዛሬ ማለዳ መጥታ ከዚያ ጀምሮ ስትሠራ ቆይታለች። ያረፈችው በመጠለያው ውስጥ ለጥቂት ጊዜ ብቻ ነው።»

decisions.choice: her sitting in the house has been little: she has hardly rested
alternatives: she has stood waiting since morning
she has not rested even a little
decisions.reason: The end of the verse is very hard in the Hebrew, word for word "this her sitting the house little". The likeliest sense is that she has kept working since morning and rested only briefly in the field shelter. Others take it to mean that she has stood waiting for permission since morning, or read it as "she has not rested in the field even a little", as the ancient Greek translation does. The wording may have been damaged in copying.

decisions.choice: gather among the sheaves: glean where the cut grain lies bundled
decisions.reason: Gleaners usually followed behind once the sheaves had been tied and taken away. Ruth asks to gather among the sheaves themselves, more than the law granted, and in verse 15 Boaz allows it. The words may also mean that she asked to gather her gleanings into bundles.

decisions.choice: the house: the field shelter
decisions.reason: In the middle of a field "the house" is most likely a simple shelter where workers rested out of the sun.

decisions.choice: on her feet ... (Balanced); working ever since (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Stood" here means she has stayed at work; Balanced and Readable say so. Literal keeps "stood".

decisions.choice: She asked me
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the foreman is reporting Ruth's own request to him.

decisions.choice: o abrigo
decisions.reason: "The house" in a field is a simple shelter (m3); "abrigo" says that plainly, where "casa" would put Ruth back in town. Literal keeps "casa" with the hard wording of m1.

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ בֹּ֨עַז אֶל־ר֜וּת הֲל֧וֹא שָׁמַ֣עַתְּ בִּתִּ֗י אַל־תֵּלְכִי֙ לִלְקֹט֙ בְּשָׂדֶ֣ה אַחֵ֔ר וְגַ֛ם לֹ֥א תַעֲבוּרִ֖י מִזֶּ֑ה וְכֹ֥ה תִדְבָּקִ֖ין עִם־נַעֲרֹתָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Boaz to Ruth, [have] you not heard, my daughter? Do not go to glean in another field, and also do not pass on from this, and thus stay close with my young women.

en.L: And Boaz said to Ruth, "Have you not heard, my daughter? Do not go to glean in another field, and also do not pass on from this [one], but keep close here to my young women.
en.B: Then Boaz said to Ruth, "Listen to me, my daughter. Do not go to glean in any other field, and do not move on from this one. Stay here close to my young women.
en.R: Boaz said to Ruth, "Listen to me, my daughter. Do not go off to pick up grain in any other field. Do not leave this one. Stay here with the young women who work for me.

sw.L: Naye Boazi akamwambia Ruthu, "Je, hujasikia, binti yangu? Usiende kuokota masazo katika shamba lingine, wala usiondoke hapa, bali ukae karibu na wasichana wangu hapa.
sw.B: Kisha Boazi alimwambia Ruthu, "Nisikilize, binti yangu. Usiende kuokota masazo katika shamba lingine lolote, wala usiondoke katika shamba hili. Kaa hapa karibu na wasichana wangu.
sw.R: Boazi alimwambia Ruthu, "Nisikilize, binti yangu. Usiende kuokota nafaka katika shamba lingine lolote. Usiliache shamba hili. Kaa hapa pamoja na wasichana wanaonifanyia kazi.

es.L: Y Booz dijo a Rut: «¿No oyes, hija mía? No vayas a recoger espigas a otro campo, y tampoco te vayas de este, sino quédate aquí junto a mis criadas.
es.B: Entonces Booz le dijo a Rut: «Escúchame, hija mía. No vayas a recoger espigas a ningún otro campo, y no te vayas de este. Quédate aquí junto a mis criadas.
es.R: Booz le dijo a Rut: «Escúchame, hija mía. No te vayas a recoger grano a ningún otro campo. No te vayas de este. Quédate aquí con las muchachas que trabajan para mí.

fr.L: Et Booz dit à Ruth : « N’entends-tu pas, ma fille ? Ne va pas glaner dans un autre champ, et ne t’éloigne pas non plus d’ici, mais reste ainsi près de mes servantes.
fr.B: Booz dit alors à Ruth : « Écoute-moi, ma fille. Ne va pas glaner dans un autre champ, et ne t’éloigne pas d’ici. Reste près de mes servantes.
fr.R: Booz a dit à Ruth : « Écoute-moi, ma fille. Ne va pas ramasser des épis dans un autre champ. Ne pars pas d’ici. Reste avec les jeunes femmes qui travaillent pour moi.

vi.L: Bô-ô nói với Ru-tơ: "Con gái ta, con không nghe sao? Đừng đi mót trong ruộng khác, cũng đừng rời khỏi đây, nhưng hãy ở gần các thiếu nữ của ta tại đây.
vi.B: Bấy giờ Bô-ô nói với Ru-tơ: "Con gái ta, hãy nghe ta nói. Đừng đi mót ở ruộng nào khác, cũng đừng rời khỏi ruộng này. Hãy ở đây gần các thiếu nữ làm việc cho ta.
vi.R: Bô-ô nói với Ru-tơ: "Con gái ta, hãy nghe ta. Đừng đi nhặt lúa ở ruộng nào khác. Đừng rời khỏi ruộng này. Hãy ở đây với các thiếu nữ làm việc cho ta.

ko.L: 보아스가 룻에게 말했다. "내 딸아, 듣지 않았느냐? 이삭을 주우러 다른 밭으로 가지 말고, 여기에서 떠나지도 말고, 여기에서 내 젊은 여자들과 가까이 있어라.
ko.B: 그러자 보아스가 룻에게 말했다. "내 딸아, 잘 들어라. 이삭을 주우러 다른 밭으로 가지 말고, 이 밭을 떠나지도 마라. 여기에서 내 여종들과 함께 있어라.
ko.R: 보아스가 룻에게 말했다. "내 딸아, 잘 들어라. 이삭을 주우러 다른 밭으로 가지 마라. 이 밭을 떠나지 마라. 여기에서 나를 위해 일하는 젊은 여자들과 함께 있어라.

pt.L: E Boaz disse a Rute: "Você não ouviu, minha filha? Não vá respigar em outro campo, e também não passe adiante daqui, mas fique assim junto das minhas moças.
pt.B: Então Boaz disse a Rute: "Escute, minha filha. Não vá respigar em nenhum outro campo e não saia daqui. Fique aqui, junto das minhas moças.
pt.R: Boaz disse a Rute: "Escute, minha filha. Não vá apanhar espigas em nenhum outro campo. Não saia deste. Fique aqui com as moças que trabalham para mim.

am.L: ቦዔዝም ሩትን አላት፦ «ልጄ ሆይ፣ አልሰማሽምን? ልትቃርሚ ወደ ሌላ እርሻ አትሂጂ፤ ደግሞም ከዚህ አትለፊ፤ እንዲሁ እዚህ ከልጃገረዶቼ ጋር ተጣበቂ።
am.B: ከዚያም ቦዔዝ ሩትን እንዲህ አላት፦ «ልጄ፣ ስሚኝ። ልትቃርሚ ወደ ሌላ እርሻ አትሂጂ፤ ከዚህም አትራቂ። እዚሁ ከልጃገረዶቼ ጋር ተጠግተሽ ቆዪ።
am.R: ቦዔዝ ሩትን እንዲህ አላት፦ «ልጄ፣ ስሚኝ። እህል ለመልቀም ወደ ሌላ እርሻ አትሂጂ። ይህን እርሻ ትተሽ አትሂጂ። ለእኔ ከሚሠሩት ወጣት ሴቶች ጋር እዚሁ ቆዪ።

decisions.choice: have you not heard?: listen to me
decisions.reason: The question is a polite way of asking for attention: "listen carefully".

decisions.choice: my daughter: an older man speaking kindly
decisions.reason: Naomi calls Ruth "my daughter" (verse 2), and Boaz does the same. It is a warm address from an older person to a younger one, and suggests that Boaz is older than Ruth (3:10).

decisions.choice: keep close: stay with, cling to
decisions.reason: The verb dabaq is the one used of Ruth clinging to Naomi (1:14). Boaz asks her to keep close to his young women, and she does (verse 23).

decisions.choice: Listen to me (Balanced); Listen (Readable)
decisions.reason: The question "have you not heard?" is given its sense; Literal keeps the question.

decisions.choice: "hija mía" for Boaz to Ruth; "tú" between Boaz and Ruth, and "mi señor" from Ruth (verse 13)
decisions.reason: Boaz speaks to Ruth as an older man speaking kindly (m2), and "hija mía" says that in Spanish too. As everywhere in this translation, one person is addressed with "tú"; Ruth's respect for Boaz is carried by "mi señor" and by her humble words, not by "usted".

decisions.choice: "tu" between Boaz and Ruth in both directions; Boaz says "ma fille", Ruth says "mon seigneur" (L, B) or "Monsieur" (R, 2:13)
alternatives: "vous" from Ruth to Boaz, as to a man of rank
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets, "tu" to one person, as modern French Bibles do; the respect between them is carried by the words of address, "ma fille" from the older man and "mon seigneur" from Ruth. Boaz's young women are "mes servantes" (L, B).

decisions.choice: Boaz says "ta" and "con" (and "con gái ta") to Ruth; she answers with "tôi" and "ông"
decisions.reason: As the Joshua–Ruth terms note sets for their first meeting: an older landowner speaking kindly, a young foreign widow answering with respect.

decisions.choice: Boaz speaks to Ruth in the plain style (해라체) with "내 딸아"; Ruth answers him in the formal polite style (합쇼체)
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set: Boaz is the older man and the landowner, and he calls her "my daughter"; Ruth, a foreigner gleaning in his field, speaks up to him.

decisions.choice: minha filha; você
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Boaz, the older man (m2), speaks to Ruth with "minha filha" and "você"; she answers him with "o senhor" and calls herself "a sua serva" where the Hebrew does (verse 13; 3:9). The difference in address shows the difference in rank the Hebrew shows.

decisions.choice: keep close: "ተጣበቂ" (Literal), the verb used of Ruth clinging to Naomi in 1:14
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the same verb (dabaq) in 1:14, here, and in 2:21, 23; Literal keeps one Amharic verb for it so the echo is visible. Balanced and Readable say "stay close" in ordinary words.

source.text: עֵינַ֜יִךְ בַּשָּׂדֶ֤ה אֲשֶׁר־יִקְצֹרוּן֙ וְהָלַ֣כְתִּאַחֲרֵיהֶ֔ן הֲל֥וֹא צִוִּ֛יתִי אֶת־הַנְּעָרִ֖ים לְבִלְתִּ֣י נָגְעֵ֑ךְ וְצָמִ֗ת וְהָלַכְתְּ֙ אֶל־הַכֵּלִ֔ים וְשָׁתִ֕ית מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר יִשְׁאֲב֖וּן הַנְּעָרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Your eyes [be] on the field which they harvest, and you will go after them. [Have] I not commanded the young men not to touch you? And [when] you are thirsty, you will go to the vessels and drink from what draw the young men.

en.L: [Let] your eyes [be] on the field that they are harvesting, and go after them. Have I not commanded the young men not to touch you? And when you are thirsty, go to the vessels and drink from what the young men draw."
en.B: Keep your eyes on the field they are harvesting, and follow along after the women. I have ordered the young men not to lay a hand on you. And when you are thirsty, go to the jars and drink from the water the young men have drawn."
en.R: Watch which field they are working in, and follow the women there. I have told the young men not to bother you. When you are thirsty, go and drink from the water jars the young men have filled."

sw.L: Macho yako [na yawe] juu ya shamba wanalovuna, uwafuate. Je, sikuwaamuru vijana wasikuguse? Nawe ukiona kiu, nenda kwenye vyombo unywe katika yale wanayoteka vijana."
sw.B: Yaangalie shamba wanalovuna, uwafuate wale wanawake. Nimewaamuru vijana wasikuguse. Nawe ukiona kiu, nenda kwenye mitungi unywe maji yaliyotekwa na vijana."
sw.R: Angalia ni shamba gani wanalofanyia kazi, uwafuate wanawake huko. Nimewaambia vijana wasikusumbue. Ukiona kiu, nenda ukanywe maji kutoka kwenye mitungi ambayo vijana wameijaza."

es.L: [Estén] tus ojos en el campo que sieguen, y ve tras ellas. ¿No he mandado a los criados que no te toquen? Y cuando tengas sed, ve a las vasijas y bebe de lo que sacan los criados».
es.B: Fíjate en el campo que están segando y sigue a las mujeres. He ordenado a los criados que no te pongan la mano encima. Y cuando tengas sed, ve a los cántaros y bebe del agua que han sacado los criados».
es.R: Fíjate en qué campo están trabajando, y sigue allí a las mujeres. Les he dicho a los muchachos que no te molesten. Cuando tengas sed, ve a beber de los cántaros de agua que los muchachos han llenado».

fr.L: [Que] tes yeux [soient] sur le champ qu’ils moissonnent, et va derrière elles. N’ai-je pas ordonné aux jeunes gens de ne pas te toucher ? Et quand tu auras soif, va vers les cruches et bois de ce que les jeunes gens auront puisé. »
fr.B: Garde les yeux sur le champ qu’on moissonne, et suis les femmes. J’ai interdit aux jeunes gens de porter la main sur toi. Et quand tu auras soif, va aux cruches et bois de l’eau que les jeunes gens auront puisée. »
fr.R: Regarde dans quel champ elles travaillent, et suis-les. J’ai dit aux jeunes hommes de ne pas t’embêter. Quand tu auras soif, va boire aux cruches que les jeunes hommes ont remplies d’eau. »

vi.L: Mắt con [hãy để] trên ruộng mà họ đang gặt, và hãy đi theo sau họ. Ta chẳng đã truyền cho các chàng trai không được đụng đến con sao? Khi con khát, hãy đến các bình mà uống nước các chàng trai đã múc."
vi.B: Hãy để ý xem họ gặt ruộng nào, rồi đi theo sau các cô ấy. Ta đã dặn các chàng trai không được đụng đến con. Khi khát, con cứ đến các vò nước mà uống nước các chàng trai đã múc."
vi.R: Hãy để ý xem họ đang gặt ở ruộng nào, rồi đi theo các cô ấy đến đó. Ta đã bảo các chàng trai không được làm phiền con. Khi khát, con cứ đến uống nước ở các vò nước các chàng trai đã múc đầy."

ko.L: 그들이 거두는 밭을 눈여겨보았다가 그들의 뒤를 따라가거라. 내가 젊은 남자들에게 너를 건드리지 말라고 명령하지 않았느냐? 목이 마르면 그릇이 있는 데로 가서 젊은 남자들이 길어 온 물을 마셔라."
ko.B: 일꾼들이 거두는 밭을 잘 보아 두었다가 여자들 뒤를 따라가거라. 내가 젊은 남자들에게 너를 건드리지 말라고 일러 두었다. 목이 마르면 물 항아리가 있는 데로 가서 젊은 남자들이 길어 온 물을 마셔라."
ko.R: 일꾼들이 어느 밭에서 일하는지 잘 보고, 여자들을 따라 그리로 가거라. 내가 젊은 남자들에게 너를 괴롭히지 말라고 말해 두었다. 목이 마르면 젊은 남자들이 채워 놓은 물 항아리에 가서 마셔라."

pt.L: [Que] os seus olhos [estejam] no campo que eles ceifarem, e vá atrás delas. Não ordenei eu aos moços que não toquem em você? E, quando tiver sede, vá aos vasos e beba do que os moços tirarem."

pt.R: Veja em que campo eles estão trabalhando e vá com as moças para lá. Eu disse aos rapazes que não mexessem com você. Quando tiver sede, vá beber dos jarros de água que os rapazes encheram."

am.L: ዓይኖችሽ በሚያጭዱት እርሻ ላይ [ይሁኑ]፤ ተከትለሻቸውም ሂጂ። ጎበዛዝቱ እንዳይነኩሽ አላዘዝኳቸውምን? በተጠማሽም ጊዜ ወደ ዕቃዎቹ ሄደሽ ጎበዛዝቱ ከቀዱት ጠጪ።»

decisions.choice: after them: after the young women
decisions.reason: The pronoun is feminine: Ruth is to follow the young women of verse 8, who come behind the reapers binding the sheaves.

decisions.choice: touch: harm or harass
decisions.reason: To "touch" someone can mean to strike, harm or molest them (Genesis 26:11, 29). A foreign woman alone in the fields could be mistreated; Naomi sees the same danger in verse 22.

decisions.choice: the young men draw water for her
decisions.reason: Water was usually drawn by women (Genesis 24:11), and a foreign gleaner might expect to serve others. Here the men of Boaz's household draw it and she drinks freely.

decisions.choice: I have ordered (Balanced); I have told (Readable)
decisions.reason: The question "have I not commanded ...?" expects the answer yes, so Balanced and Readable state it plainly; Literal keeps the question.

decisions.choice: the women; the water
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who "them" is and what is drawn.

decisions.choice: atrás delas
decisions.reason: Portuguese "delas" shows what the feminine pronoun of m1 shows, that Ruth follows the young women, so Literal needs no supplied noun; Balanced and Readable name "as moças", as the English does.

records.literal_gloss: And she fell on her face and bowed down to [the] ground and said to him, why have I found favor in your eyes, to take notice of me, and I [am] a foreigner?

en.L: And she fell on her face and bowed down to the ground and said to him, "Why have I found favor in your eyes, that you take notice of me, when I [am] a foreigner?"
en.B: Ruth fell face down and bowed to the ground. She said to him, "Why have I found such favor with you, that you would take notice of me, when I am a foreigner?"
en.R: Ruth bowed down with her face to the ground. She said to him, "Why are you so kind to me? Why do you care about me? I am a foreigner."

sw.L: Naye akaanguka kifudifudi, akainama mpaka chini, akamwambia, "Kwa nini nimepata kibali machoni pako, hata unanijali, nami ni mgeni?"
sw.B: Ruthu alianguka kifudifudi, akainama mpaka chini. Akamwambia, "Kwa nini nimepata kibali kama hiki kwako, hata unanijali, nami ni mgeni?"
sw.R: Ruthu aliinama mpaka uso wake ukagusa chini. Alimwambia, "Kwa nini unanitendea wema namna hii? Kwa nini unanijali? Mimi ni mgeni."

es.L: Y ella cayó sobre su rostro y se inclinó a tierra y le dijo: «¿Por qué he hallado gracia a tus ojos, para que te fijes en mí, siendo yo extranjera?».
es.B: Rut se postró rostro en tierra y le dijo: «¿Por qué me miras con tanto favor, que te fijas en mí, siendo yo una extranjera?».
es.R: Rut se inclinó con el rostro en tierra. Le dijo: «¿Por qué eres tan bueno conmigo? ¿Por qué te preocupas por mí? Yo soy extranjera».

fr.L: Et elle tomba sur sa face et se prosterna jusqu’à terre, et elle lui dit : « Pourquoi ai-je trouvé grâce à tes yeux, pour que tu fasses attention à moi, alors que je [suis] une étrangère ? »
fr.B: Ruth tomba face contre terre et se prosterna. Elle lui dit : « Pourquoi ai-je trouvé une telle faveur auprès de toi, que tu fasses attention à moi, moi qui suis une étrangère ? »
fr.R: Ruth s’est inclinée jusqu’à terre. Elle lui a dit : « Pourquoi es-tu si bon avec moi ? Pourquoi t’occupes-tu de moi ? Je suis une étrangère. »

vi.L: Nàng sấp mặt xuống, cúi lạy sát đất và nói với ông: "Sao tôi được ơn trước mắt ông, để ông lưu ý đến tôi, trong khi tôi [là] một người ngoại quốc?"
vi.B: Ru-tơ sấp mặt cúi lạy sát đất và nói với ông: "Sao tôi lại được ông ưu đãi như vậy, để ông lưu tâm đến tôi, trong khi tôi chỉ là một người ngoại quốc?"
vi.R: Ru-tơ cúi lạy, mặt sát đất. Nàng nói với ông: "Sao ông lại tử tế với tôi như vậy? Sao ông lại quan tâm đến tôi? Tôi là người ngoại quốc mà."

ko.L: 룻이 얼굴을 땅에 대고 엎드려 절하며 그에게 말했다. "제가 이방 여자인데, 어찌하여 제가 주인님의 눈에 은혜를 입어 주인님께서 저를 이렇게 돌보아 주십니까?"
ko.B: 룻은 얼굴을 땅에 대고 엎드려 절하며 말했다. "저는 이방 여자인데, 어찌하여 주인님께서 저를 이렇게 좋게 보시고 돌보아 주십니까?"
ko.R: 룻은 얼굴을 땅에 대고 절했다. 룻이 보아스에게 말했다. "왜 저에게 이렇게 친절하십니까? 왜 저를 이렇게 생각해 주십니까? 저는 외국 여자입니다."

pt.L: E ela caiu sobre o seu rosto, e se prostrou em terra, e lhe disse: "Por que encontrei favor aos seus olhos, para que o senhor repare em mim, sendo eu uma estrangeira?"
pt.B: Rute se prostrou com o rosto em terra e lhe disse: "Por que encontrei tanto favor diante do senhor, a ponto de o senhor reparar em mim, sendo eu uma estrangeira?"
pt.R: Rute se curvou até o chão e disse a Boaz: "Por que o senhor é tão bondoso comigo? Por que se importa comigo? Eu sou uma estrangeira."

am.L: እርሷም በግንባሯ ተደፍታ ወደ መሬት ሰገደች፤ እንዲህም አለችው፦ «እኔ ባዕድ ሆኜ ሳለሁ ያስተውሉኝ ዘንድ በዓይንዎ ሞገስ ያገኘሁት ስለ ምንድን ነው?»
am.B: ሩትም በግንባሯ ተደፍታ እስከ መሬት ሰገደች። እርሱንም፦ «እኔ ባዕድ ሆኜ ሳለሁ እንዲህ የሚያስቡልኝ፣ በፊትዎ እንዲህ ያለ ሞገስ ያገኘሁት ለምንድን ነው?» አለችው።
am.R: ሩት በፊቷ ወደ መሬት ተደፍታ ሰገደች። እርሱንም፦ «ለምን እንዲህ ደግ ሆኑልኝ? ለምንስ ያስቡልኛል? እኔ እኮ የውጭ አገር ሰው ነኝ» አለችው።

decisions.choice: take notice of me ... a foreigner: a play on words
decisions.reason: "Take notice of" (hakkir) and "foreigner" (nokhriyyah) sound alike in Hebrew. A foreigner was someone others did not recognize or care about, yet Boaz has recognized her.

decisions.choice: foreigner: one from another people
decisions.reason: Nokhriyyah is a foreign woman, an outsider with no place in Israel by birth, a stronger word than the ger who has settled among the people. Ruth expects nothing as a Moabite (Deuteronomy 23:4).

decisions.choice: fell on her face and bowed: deep respect and thanks
decisions.reason: Bowing to the ground was the way to honor a superior and thank him (1 Samuel 25:23).

decisions.choice: two questions and a statement
decisions.reason: Readable divides the long question into short ones; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: "mgeni" for the foreigner (nokhri)
decisions.reason: Swahili "mgeni" is the ordinary word for someone from elsewhere; the Hebrew play between "take notice of" and "foreigner" (m1) cannot be kept, and the meaning decision explains it.

decisions.choice: "te fijes en mí" ... "extranjera"; the play on words is not kept
decisions.reason: In Hebrew "take notice of" and "foreigner" are built from the same letters (m1). Spanish cannot keep both meanings and the sound; it keeps the meanings, and the meaning decision tells the reader of the play.

decisions.choice: "lưu ý / lưu tâm đến" and "người ngoại quốc", without the Hebrew wordplay
decisions.reason: In Hebrew "take notice of" and "foreigner" sound alike (meaning decision); Vietnamese cannot keep the play, so it keeps the plain sense.

decisions.choice: reparar em mim ... uma estrangeira
decisions.reason: For the whole book: nokhriyyah (m2), the foreign woman with no place in Israel, is "estrangeira" at every level, kept apart from "imigrante", the word for the ger who has settled among the people (1:1). Portuguese cannot echo the sound play of m1; "reparar em" is kept for "take notice of" here and in verse 19, so Naomi's blessing repeats Ruth's words as in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: Ruth to Boaz with the respectful "እርስዎ" ("በዓይንዎ", "ያስተውሉኝ", "ሆኑልኝ"), here and through the book
decisions.reason: A foreign widow gleaning in his field speaks up to the landowner, who answers her as an older kinsman with "አንቺ" and "ልጄ" (terms list for Joshua to 2 Samuel). The play on words between "take notice of" and "foreigner" (meaning decision m1) has no Amharic match and is left to that decision.

source.text: וַיַּ֤עַן בֹּ֨עַז֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָ֔הּ הֻגֵּ֨ד הֻגַּ֜ד לִ֗י כֹּ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂית֙ אֶת־חֲמוֹתֵ֔ךְ אַחֲרֵ֖י מ֣וֹת אִישֵׁ֑ךְ וַתַּֽעַזְבִ֞י אָּבִ֣יךְוְאִמֵּ֗ךְ וְאֶ֨רֶץ֙ מֽוֹלַדְתֵּ֔ךְ וַתֵּ֣לְכִ֔י אֶל־עַ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־יָדַ֖עַתְּ תְּמ֥וֹל שִׁלְשֽׁוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered Boaz and said to her, told, it has been told to me all that you have done with your mother-in-law after [the] death of your husband, and you left your father and your mother and [the] land of your birth and you came to a people that you did not know yesterday three days ago.

en.L: And Boaz answered and said to her, "It has been fully told to me, all that you have done for your mother-in-law after the death of your husband, and [how] you left your father and your mother and the land of your birth, and came to a people whom you did not know yesterday [or] the day before.
en.B: Boaz answered her, "I have heard the whole story of what you have done for your mother-in-law after your husband's death: how you left your father and mother and the land where you were born, and came to a people you had never known before.
en.R: Boaz answered, "People have told me how good you have been to your mother-in-law since your husband died. You left your father and mother and the country where you were born. You came to live among people you did not know before.

sw.L: Naye Boazi akajibu, akamwambia, "Nimeambiwa kikamilifu yote uliyomtendea mama mkwe wako baada ya kifo cha mumeo, na [jinsi] ulivyomwacha baba yako na mama yako na nchi ya kuzaliwa kwako, ukaja kwa watu usiowajua jana [wala] juzi.
sw.B: Boazi alimjibu, "Nimesikia habari yote ya yale uliyomtendea mama mkwe wako tangu mumeo alipokufa: jinsi ulivyomwacha baba yako na mama yako na nchi uliyozaliwa, ukaja kwa watu ambao hukuwahi kuwajua kabla.
sw.R: Boazi alijibu, "Watu wameniambia jinsi ulivyokuwa mwema kwa mama mkwe wako tangu mumeo alipokufa. Ulimwacha baba yako na mama yako na nchi uliyozaliwa. Ulikuja kuishi kati ya watu usiowajua kabla.

es.L: Y Booz respondió y le dijo: «Se me ha contado bien todo lo que has hecho con tu suegra después de la muerte de tu marido, y [cómo] dejaste a tu padre y a tu madre y la tierra de tu nacimiento, y viniste a un pueblo que no conocías ni ayer ni anteayer.
es.B: Booz le respondió: «Me han contado todo lo que has hecho por tu suegra desde que murió tu marido: cómo dejaste a tu padre y a tu madre y la tierra donde naciste, y viniste a un pueblo que antes no conocías.
es.R: Booz le contestó: «Me han contado lo buena que has sido con tu suegra desde que murió tu esposo. Dejaste a tu padre y a tu madre y el país donde naciste. Viniste a vivir entre gente que antes no conocías.

fr.L: Et Booz répondit et lui dit : « On m’a raconté, raconté, tout ce que tu as fait pour ta belle-mère depuis la mort de ton mari, et [comment] tu as quitté ton père et ta mère et le pays de ta naissance, et tu es venue vers un peuple que tu ne connaissais ni hier ni avant-hier.
fr.B: Booz lui répondit : « On m’a raconté en détail tout ce que tu as fait pour ta belle-mère depuis la mort de ton mari : comment tu as quitté ton père, ta mère et le pays où tu es née, pour venir vers un peuple que tu ne connaissais pas auparavant.
fr.R: Booz a répondu : « On m’a raconté comme tu as été bonne pour ta belle-mère depuis la mort de ton mari. Tu as quitté ton père et ta mère et le pays où tu es née. Tu es venue vivre chez des gens que tu ne connaissais pas avant.

vi.L: Bô-ô đáp lời nàng: "Người ta đã kể hết cho ta mọi điều con đã làm cho mẹ chồng con sau khi chồng con chết, và [việc] con đã bỏ cha mẹ và quê hương mình mà đến với một dân tộc con chưa từng biết trước đây.
vi.B: Bô-ô đáp: "Ta đã nghe kể hết mọi điều con đã làm cho mẹ chồng từ khi chồng con qua đời: con đã bỏ cha mẹ và quê hương nơi con sinh ra, mà đến với một dân tộc con chưa từng biết trước đây.
vi.R: Bô-ô trả lời: "Người ta đã kể cho ta nghe con đã tốt với mẹ chồng thế nào từ khi chồng con qua đời. Con đã bỏ cha mẹ và đất nước nơi con sinh ra. Con đã đến sống giữa những người con chưa từng quen biết.

ko.L: 보아스가 대답하여 그에게 말했다. "네가 남편이 죽은 뒤에 시어머니에게 한 모든 일과, 네가 네 아버지와 어머니와 네가 태어난 땅을 떠나 전에 알지 못하던 백성에게로 온 일을 내가 다 자세히 들었다.
ko.B: 보아스가 대답했다. "네 남편이 죽은 뒤에 네가 시어머니에게 한 일을 내가 다 들었다. 네가 아버지와 어머니와 고향 땅을 떠나, 전에는 알지도 못하던 백성에게로 온 것도 다 들었다.
ko.R: 보아스가 대답했다. "네 남편이 죽은 뒤에 네가 시어머니에게 얼마나 잘했는지 사람들이 나에게 말해 주었다. 너는 아버지와 어머니와 네가 태어난 나라를 떠났다. 그리고 전에 알지 못하던 사람들 가운데 와서 살고 있다.

pt.L: E Boaz respondeu e lhe disse: "Foi-me contado por inteiro tudo o que você fez pela sua sogra depois da morte do seu marido, e [como] você deixou o seu pai e a sua mãe e a terra do seu nascimento, e veio para um povo que você não conhecia ontem [nem] anteontem.
pt.B: Boaz lhe respondeu: "Contaram-me em detalhes tudo o que você fez pela sua sogra depois que o seu marido morreu: como você deixou o seu pai, a sua mãe e a terra onde nasceu e veio para um povo que você nunca tinha conhecido.
pt.R: Boaz respondeu: "As pessoas me contaram como você tem sido boa para a sua sogra desde que o seu marido morreu. Você deixou o seu pai e a sua mãe e o país onde nasceu. Veio morar no meio de um povo que você não conhecia antes.

am.L: ቦዔዝም መልሶ እንዲህ አላት፦ «ባልሽ ከሞተ በኋላ ለአማትሽ ያደረግሽው ሁሉ፣ አባትሽንና እናትሽን የተወለድሽበትንም ምድር ትተሽ ትናንትና ከትናንት ወዲያ ወደማታውቂው ሕዝብ እንደ መጣሽ በሚገባ ተነግሮኛል።
am.B: ቦዔዝም እንዲህ ብሎ መለሰላት፦ «ባልሽ ከሞተ በኋላ ለአማትሽ ያደረግሽውን ሁሉ ሰምቻለሁ፤ አባትሽንና እናትሽን የተወለድሽበትንም አገር ትተሽ ከዚህ በፊት ወደማታውቂው ሕዝብ እንዴት እንደ መጣሽ ተነግሮኛል።
am.R: ቦዔዝም እንዲህ አላት፦ «ባልሽ ከሞተ ጀምሮ ለአማትሽ ምን ያህል መልካም እንደ ሆንሽ ሰዎች ነግረውኛል። አባትሽንና እናትሽን የተወለድሽበትንም አገር ትተሽ መጥተሻል። ከዚህ በፊት በማታውቂያቸው ሰዎች መካከል ለመኖር መጣሽ።

decisions.choice: it has been fully told: the verb doubled
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the verb for emphasis: Boaz has heard the whole story, and in detail.

decisions.choice: left father, mother and the land of her birth
decisions.reason: The words recall God's call to Abraham to leave his land, his kindred and his father's house (Genesis 12:1). Ruth has made the same kind of break, with no promise given to her.

decisions.choice: yesterday, three days ago: before, in the past
decisions.reason: The pair of time words is a fixed way of saying "previously" (Genesis 31:2). She came to a people who had been strangers to her.

decisions.choice: never known before (Balanced); did not know before (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the time idiom; Literal keeps "yesterday [or] the day before".

es.L: Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} recompense tu obra, y que tu salario sea completo de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, Dios de Israel, bajo cuyas alas has venido a refugiarte».

decisions.choice: under whose wings: in God's protecting care
decisions.reason: The picture is of a bird sheltering its young under its wings (Deuteronomy 32:11; Psalm 17:8; 36:8; 91:4). The word for wing, kanaf, also means the corner of a garment, and it comes back in 3:9, where Ruth asks Boaz to spread his "wing" over her. The man who prays for her shelter becomes the one through whom it comes.

decisions.choice: wages: the pay due to a worker
decisions.reason: Maskoret is a worker's wage (Genesis 29:15; 31:7), a fitting word in a harvest field. "Repay" and "complete" also come from one root (shalem): Boaz prays that God will pay her in full.

decisions.choice: take refuge: trust oneself to God for protection
decisions.reason: To take refuge in God is to rely on him for safety (Psalm 2:12; 5:12). By coming with Naomi and taking her God as her own (1:16), Ruth has put herself under the care of the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: order of the clauses
decisions.reason: Readable says first that Ruth has come to the LORD for safety, then gives the wish for her reward, in shorter sentences.

decisions.choice: "bajo cuyas alas" at every level
decisions.reason: The picture of God's wings (m1) is kept at every level, as in the English, because Ruth 3:9 picks it up again when Ruth asks Boaz to spread his "ala" over her.

decisions.choice: "dưới cánh" for "under whose wings"
decisions.reason: The picture of a bird sheltering its young is kept at every level, because 3:9 takes up the same word when Ruth asks Boaz to spread his "wing" over her (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: sob as asas, debaixo das asas (every level)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps "asas", because the same word kanaf returns in 3:9, where Ruth asks Boaz to spread his "asa" (Literal) or "a aba do seu manto" over her (m1): the man who prays for her refuge under God's wings is asked to become that refuge. Readable adds "proteção" to make the picture plain.

decisions.choice: "ክንፎች" (wings) at every level, kept so that Ruth's request in 3:9 ("ክንፍዎን … ይዘርጉ") answers it
decisions.reason: Boaz prays that Ruth find refuge under the LORD's wings; at the threshing floor she asks him to spread his own "wing" (kanaf) over her. Amharic "ክንፍ" can carry both pictures, so the image stays at every level and Readable adds "ጥበቃ" (safety) to make the sense plain.

source.text: וַ֠תֹּאמֶר אֶמְצָא־חֵ֨ן בְּעֵינֶ֤יךָ אֲדֹנִי֙ כִּ֣י נִֽחַמְתָּ֔נִי וְכִ֥י דִבַּ֖רְתָּ עַל־לֵ֣ב שִׁפְחָתֶ֑ךָ וְאָנֹכִי֙ לֹ֣א אֶֽהְיֶ֔ה כְּאַחַ֖ת שִׁפְחֹתֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said, let me find favor in your eyes, my lord, for you have comforted me and for you have spoken to [the] heart of your maidservant, and I, I am not like one of your maidservants.

en.L: And she said, "May I find favor in your eyes, my lord, for you have comforted me and spoken to the heart of your maidservant, though I am not like one of your maidservants."
en.B: She said, "May I go on finding favor in your eyes, my lord. You have comforted me and spoken kindly to your servant, though I am not even one of your servant women."
en.R: Ruth said, "Sir, I hope you will always be this kind to me. You have comforted me. You have spoken kindly to me, and I am not even one of your servants."

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Nipate kibali machoni pako, bwana wangu, kwa maana umenifariji, na umesema na moyo wa mjakazi wako, ingawa mimi si kama mmoja wa wajakazi wako."
sw.B: Akasema, "Niendelee kupata kibali machoni pako, bwana wangu. Umenifariji na kusema kwa upole na mtumishi wako, ingawa mimi si hata mmoja wa wajakazi wako."
sw.R: Ruthu alisema, "Bwana, natumaini utaendelea kunitendea wema namna hii. Umenifariji. Umesema nami kwa upole, nami si hata mmoja wa watumishi wako."

es.L: Y ella dijo: «Halle yo gracia a tus ojos, señor mío, porque me has consolado y has hablado al corazón de tu sierva, aunque yo no soy como una de tus siervas».
es.B: Ella dijo: «Que siga yo hallando favor a tus ojos, señor mío. Me has consolado y le has hablado con bondad a tu sierva, aunque ni siquiera soy una de tus siervas».
es.R: Rut le dijo: «Señor, espero que siempre seas así de bueno conmigo. Me has consolado. Me has hablado con bondad, aunque ni siquiera soy una de tus sirvientas».

fr.L: Et elle dit : « Que je trouve grâce à tes yeux, mon seigneur, car tu m’as consolée et tu as parlé au cœur de ta servante, alors que moi, je ne suis pas comme l’une de tes servantes. »
fr.B: Elle dit : « Puissé-je continuer à trouver grâce à tes yeux, mon seigneur ! Tu m’as consolée et tu as parlé avec bonté à ta servante, alors que je ne suis même pas l’une de tes servantes. »
fr.R: Ruth a dit : « Monsieur, j’espère que tu seras toujours aussi bon avec moi. Tu m’as consolée. Tu m’as parlé avec gentillesse, et pourtant je ne suis même pas l’une de tes servantes. »

vi.L: Nàng nói: "Thưa ông, nguyện tôi được ơn trước mắt ông, vì ông đã an ủi tôi và nói với lòng của tớ gái ông, dù tôi không bằng một trong các tớ gái của ông."
vi.B: Nàng nói: "Thưa ông, mong rằng tôi luôn được ông đoái thương. Ông đã an ủi tôi và nói những lời dịu dàng với đầy tớ gái của ông, dù tôi còn chẳng phải là một trong những đầy tớ gái của ông."
vi.R: Ru-tơ nói: "Thưa ông, tôi mong ông sẽ luôn tử tế với tôi như vậy. Ông đã an ủi tôi. Ông đã nói những lời tử tế với tôi, dù tôi còn chẳng phải là người làm của ông."

ko.L: 룻이 말했다. "제 주인님, 제가 주인님의 눈에 은혜를 입기를 바랍니다. 저는 주인님의 여종 가운데 하나만도 못한데, 주인님께서 저를 위로하시고 이 여종의 마음에 말씀해 주셨습니다."
ko.B: 룻이 말했다. "주인님, 앞으로도 저를 좋게 보아 주십시오. 저는 주인님의 여종 축에도 끼지 못하는데, 주인님께서 저를 위로하시고 이 여종에게 다정하게 말씀해 주셨습니다."
ko.R: 룻이 말했다. "주인님, 앞으로도 저에게 이렇게 친절하게 대해 주시기를 바랍니다. 주인님께서 저를 위로해 주셨습니다. 저는 주인님의 종도 아닌데, 저에게 다정하게 말씀해 주셨습니다."

pt.L: E ela disse: "Que eu encontre favor aos seus olhos, meu senhor, pois o senhor me consolou e falou ao coração da sua criada, embora eu não seja como uma das suas criadas."
pt.B: Ela disse: "Que eu continue a encontrar favor aos seus olhos, meu senhor. O senhor me consolou e falou com bondade à sua serva, embora eu não seja nem mesmo uma das suas criadas."
pt.R: Rute disse: "Senhor, espero que o senhor continue sempre tão bondoso comigo. O senhor me consolou. Falou comigo com bondade, e eu nem sou uma das suas criadas."

am.L: እርሷም አለች፦ «ጌታዬ ሆይ፣ አጽናንተውኛልና፣ ለገረድዎም ልብ [የሚደርስ ቃል] ተናግረዋልና፣ በዓይንዎ ሞገስ ላግኝ፤ እኔ ግን ከገረዶችዎ እንደ አንዷ አይደለሁም።»
am.B: እርሷም፦ «ጌታዬ ሆይ፣ በፊትዎ ሞገስ ማግኘቴ ይቀጥል። እኔ ከሴት አገልጋዮችዎ እንደ አንዷ እንኳ ሳልሆን አጽናንተውኛል፤ ለአገልጋይዎም በደግነት ተናግረዋል» አለች።
am.R: ሩትም፦ «ጌታዬ፣ ሁልጊዜ እንዲህ ደግ እንዲሆኑልኝ እመኛለሁ። አጽናንተውኛል። ከአገልጋዮችዎ አንዷ እንኳ ሳልሆን በደግነት አነጋግረውኛል» አለች።

decisions.choice: may I find favor: a wish, or thanks
alternatives: I have found favor in your eyes
decisions.reason: The verb can be read as a wish ("may I find favor", that is, may your kindness continue) or as a grateful statement ("I am finding favor with you"). Either way she is thanking him.

decisions.choice: spoken to the heart: spoken kindly, reassured
decisions.reason: To speak to someone's heart is to speak words of comfort and encouragement (Genesis 50:21; Isaiah 40:2).

decisions.choice: maidservant: shifchah, a female servant of low rank
decisions.reason: Shifchah is a servant girl, one of the household's workers. Ruth calls herself his shifchah out of humility, yet says she does not even rank with his servant women. In 3:9 she calls herself his 'amah, a servant woman who could become a wife.

decisions.choice: servant, servant women (Balanced); servants (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "maidservant"; Balanced and Readable use the plain word.

decisions.choice: Sir
decisions.reason: "My lord" is a polite address to a man of higher rank, not a title for God; Readable says "Sir".

decisions.choice: "Thưa ông" for "my lord"; "tớ gái" (L), "đầy tớ gái" (B) for *shifhah*
decisions.reason: Ruth speaks of herself as a servant of the lowest rank (meaning decision); "thưa ông" is the respectful address the Genesis note gives for *adoni* to a man.

decisions.choice: "주인님" for "my lord" and "이 여종" for Ruth's "your maidservant"
decisions.reason: Ruth addresses Boaz as a woman of low standing addresses a landowner; Korean "주인님" fits that respect without implying he is her master in law.

decisions.choice: a sua criada (L), a sua serva (B); as suas criadas (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Shifchah (m3) is a servant girl of low rank: "criada" at Literal, and for his servant women at every level. Balanced says "a sua serva" where Ruth speaks of herself, the courtly way a woman spoke of herself to a superior; in 3:9 she uses 'amah, "a sua serva" at every level, so Literal keeps the two Hebrew words apart.

decisions.choice: Ruth calls herself "ገረድዎ" (Literal), "አገልጋይዎ" (Balanced); her lord "ጌታዬ" at every level
decisions.reason: The courtly self-description of the terms list ("ባሪያዎ" Literal, "አገልጋይዎ" Balanced and Readable, with the respectful -ዎ of "እርስዎ") takes its feminine form: "ገረድ" is the Amharic word for a maidservant. The same pair stands for her other word, ʾamah, in 3:9.

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ לָ֨ה בֹ֜עַז לְעֵ֣ת הָאֹ֗כֶל גֹּ֤שִֽׁי הֲלֹם֙ וְאָכַ֣לְתְּ מִן־הַלֶּ֔חֶם וְטָבַ֥לְתְּ פִּתֵּ֖ךְ בַּחֹ֑מֶץ וַתֵּ֨שֶׁב֙ מִצַּ֣ד הַקּֽוֹצְרִ֔ים וַיִּצְבָּט־לָ֣הּ קָלִ֔י וַתֹּ֥אכַל וַתִּשְׂבַּ֖ע וַתֹּתַֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to her Boaz at [the] time of the meal, come near here and eat from the bread and dip your morsel in the vinegar. And she sat at [the] side of the harvesters, and he held out to her roasted grain, and she ate and was satisfied and had left over.

en.L: And Boaz said to her at the time of the meal, "Come near here and eat some of the bread, and dip your piece in the vinegar." So she sat beside the harvesters, and he held out roasted grain to her, and she ate and was satisfied and had some left over.
en.B: When mealtime came, Boaz said to her, "Come over here and help yourself to some bread. Dip your piece in the sour wine." So she sat down beside the harvesters, and he passed her some roasted grain. She ate all she wanted and still had some left over.
en.R: When it was time to eat, Boaz said to Ruth, "Come here and eat some bread. Dip it in the sour wine." So Ruth sat down with the harvesters, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. She ate until she was full, and there was still some left over.

sw.L: Naye Boazi akamwambia wakati wa kula, "Karibia hapa, ule mkate, na uchovye kipande chako katika siki." Basi akaketi kando ya wavunaji, naye akampa bisi, naye akala, akashiba, akabakiza.
sw.B: Wakati wa chakula ulipofika, Boazi alimwambia, "Njoo hapa ujipatie mkate. Chovya kipande chako katika divai chachu." Basi aliketi kando ya wavunaji, naye akampa bisi. Alikula akashiba, na bado akabakiza.
sw.R: Wakati wa kula ulipofika, Boazi alimwambia Ruthu, "Njoo hapa ule mkate. Uchovye katika divai chachu." Kwa hiyo Ruthu aliketi pamoja na wavunaji, naye Boazi akampa bisi. Alikula mpaka akashiba, na bado vikabaki vingine.

es.L: Y Booz le dijo a la hora de la comida: «Acércate aquí y come del pan, y moja tu bocado en el vinagre». Y ella se sentó junto a los segadores, y él le ofreció grano tostado, y ella comió y se sació y le sobró.
es.B: Cuando llegó la hora de comer, Booz le dijo: «Ven aquí y sírvete pan. Moja tu bocado en el vino agrio». Así que ella se sentó junto a los segadores, y él le pasó grano tostado. Comió todo lo que quiso, y todavía le sobró.
es.R: Cuando llegó la hora de comer, Booz le dijo a Rut: «Ven aquí a comer pan. Mójalo en el vino agrio». Rut se sentó con los segadores, y Booz le dio grano tostado. Ella comió hasta quedar satisfecha, y todavía le sobró.

fr.L: Et Booz lui dit au moment du repas : « Approche-toi d’ici, et mange du pain, et trempe ton morceau dans le vinaigre. » Et elle s’assit à côté des moissonneurs, et il lui tendit du grain grillé, et elle mangea et fut rassasiée et en garda le reste.
fr.B: À l’heure du repas, Booz lui dit : « Viens ici, sers-toi de pain et trempe ton morceau dans la piquette. » Elle s’assit donc à côté des moissonneurs, et il lui passa du grain grillé. Elle en mangea à sa faim, et il lui en resta.
fr.R: Quand ce fut l’heure de manger, Booz a dit à Ruth : « Viens ici, mange du pain. Trempe-le dans le vin aigre. » Ruth s’est donc assise avec les moissonneurs, et Booz lui a donné du grain grillé. Elle a mangé jusqu’à ce qu’elle n’ait plus faim, et il en restait encore.

vi.L: Đến giờ ăn, Bô-ô nói với nàng: "Hãy lại đây, ăn bánh và chấm miếng bánh của con vào giấm." Vậy nàng ngồi bên cạnh những người gặt, và ông đưa cho nàng hạt lúa rang; nàng ăn no và còn dư lại.
vi.B: Đến giờ ăn, Bô-ô bảo nàng: "Lại đây ăn bánh với chúng ta. Chấm miếng bánh vào rượu chua." Vậy nàng ngồi xuống bên cạnh những người gặt, và ông đưa cho nàng ít hạt lúa rang. Nàng ăn no nê mà vẫn còn dư.
vi.R: Đến giờ ăn, Bô-ô nói với Ru-tơ: "Lại đây ăn bánh. Chấm bánh vào rượu chua." Vậy Ru-tơ ngồi xuống với những người gặt, và Bô-ô đưa cho nàng ít hạt lúa rang. Nàng ăn no mà vẫn còn dư.

ko.L: 식사할 때가 되자 보아스가 룻에게 말했다. "이리 가까이 와서 빵을 먹고, 네 빵 조각을 초에 찍어 먹어라." 룻이 거두는 사람들 곁에 앉자, 보아스가 볶은 곡식을 건네주었다. 룻은 배불리 먹고도 남았다.
ko.B: 식사 때가 되자 보아스가 룻에게 말했다. "이리 와서 빵을 먹어라. 빵 조각을 신 포도주에 찍어 먹어라." 그래서 룻이 일꾼들 곁에 앉자, 보아스가 볶은 곡식을 건네주었다. 룻은 배불리 먹고도 얼마를 남겼다.
ko.R: 먹을 때가 되자 보아스가 룻에게 말했다. "이리 와서 빵을 좀 먹어라. 신 포도주에 찍어 먹어라." 그래서 룻은 일꾼들과 함께 앉았고, 보아스는 볶은 곡식을 룻에게 건네주었다. 룻은 배부르게 먹었는데도 먹을 것이 남았다.

pt.L: E Boaz lhe disse na hora da refeição: "Chegue-se aqui, e coma do pão, e molhe o seu pedaço no vinagre." E ela se sentou ao lado dos ceifeiros, e ele lhe ofereceu grãos tostados, e ela comeu, e se saciou, e ainda lhe sobrou.
pt.B: Na hora da refeição, Boaz lhe disse: "Venha cá e sirva-se de pão. Molhe o seu pedaço no vinho azedo." Então ela se sentou ao lado dos ceifeiros, e ele lhe passou grãos tostados. Ela comeu à vontade e ainda lhe sobrou.
pt.R: Na hora de comer, Boaz disse a Rute: "Venha cá e coma um pouco de pão. Molhe no vinho azedo." Então Rute se sentou com os ceifeiros, e Boaz lhe deu grãos tostados. Ela comeu até ficar satisfeita, e ainda sobrou comida.

am.L: በምግብም ሰዓት ቦዔዝ፦ «ወደዚህ ቅረቢ፤ ከእንጀራውም ብዪ፤ ቁራሽሽንም በሆምጣጤው ንከሪ» አላት። እርሷም በአጫጆቹ አጠገብ ተቀመጠች፤ እርሱም ቆሎ አቀበላት፤ በላችም፤ ጠገበችም፤ አተረፈችም።
am.B: የምሳ ሰዓት በደረሰ ጊዜ ቦዔዝ፦ «ወደዚህ ነዪና እንጀራ ብዪ፤ ቁራሽሽንም በኮመጠጠው የወይን ጠጅ ንከሪ» አላት። ስለዚህ በአጫጆቹ አጠገብ ተቀመጠች፤ እርሱም ቆሎ ሰጣት። የፈለገችውን ያህል በልታ ጠገበች፤ ገናም ተረፋት።
am.R: የምግብ ሰዓት ሲደርስ ቦዔዝ ሩትን፦ «ወደዚህ ነዪና እንጀራ ብዪ። በኮመጠጠው የወይን ጠጅ ውስጥ ነክረሽ ብዪ» አላት። ሩትም ከአጫጆቹ ጋር ተቀመጠች፤ ቦዔዝም ቆሎ ሰጣት። እስክትጠግብ ድረስ በላች፤ ገናም ተረፋት።

decisions.choice: vinegar: a sour wine drink or dip
decisions.reason: Chomets is wine gone sour (Numbers 6:3). Workers dipped bread in it; it was a cheap, refreshing part of a field meal.

decisions.choice: roasted grain: heads of grain parched over a fire
decisions.reason: Fresh ears roasted over a fire were common food at harvest time and on a journey (Leviticus 23:14; 1 Samuel 17:17).

decisions.choice: ate and was satisfied and had left over: plenty after emptiness
decisions.reason: Naomi came home "empty" (1:21). Now Ruth eats her fill and has food to spare, which she takes home to Naomi (verse 18).

decisions.choice: sour wine
decisions.reason: "Vinegar" suggests a kitchen liquid to most readers; Balanced and Readable say what it was. Literal keeps "vinegar".

decisions.choice: "la piquette" (B); "le vin aigre" (R); "le vinaigre" (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word names a sour wine used as a drink or a dip (m1). Literal keeps "vinaigre", the word's usual sense; Balanced says "piquette", the French word for a thin, sour wine, and Readable describes it plainly, as the English says "sour wine".

decisions.choice: roasted grain "ቆሎ"; the dip "ሆምጣጤ" (Literal), "የኮመጠጠ የወይን ጠጅ" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "ቆሎ", grain parched over a fire, is still eaten in Ethiopia and is exactly what the Hebrew names. Literal keeps the word for vinegar; the other levels say what it was, a sour wine, as the English does.

decisions.choice: even among the sheaves: beyond the usual right
decisions.reason: Boaz grants what Ruth asked for (verse 7). Gleaners normally worked only where the reapers had already cleared the field; among the sheaves they could be suspected of taking the owner's grain.

decisions.choice: do not put her to shame: do not insult or humiliate her
decisions.reason: The verb means to shame or humiliate someone, by words or by treatment (1 Samuel 25:7, 15). No one is to treat her as a thief or an intruder.

decisions.choice: to go back to work

decisions.choice: pull, pull out: on purpose
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis: the reapers are to pull stalks out deliberately and drop them for her.

decisions.choice: bundles: handfuls of cut stalks
decisions.reason: Tsevatim, found only here, are the handfuls a reaper gathers before they are tied into sheaves.

decisions.choice: leave them: generosity beyond the law
decisions.reason: The law said a forgotten sheaf was to be left for the poor (Deuteronomy 24:19). Boaz tells his men to leave grain for Ruth on purpose, going beyond what the law required.

decisions.choice: on purpose
decisions.reason: Readable expresses the doubled verb with "on purpose"; Balanced uses "even", Literal "be sure to".

decisions.choice: os punhados
decisions.reason: Tsevatim (m2) are the handfuls a reaper holds before they are tied; "punhados" says that, and keeps them apart from "os feixes" of verse 15. Literal renders the doubled verb (m1) with "tirem bem tirados", Portuguese's own way of doubling a verb for emphasis.
